pattern.crimePattern: fish supplier kills the restaurant owner who exposed his frozen imported fish as fake "fresh lake fish"
pattern.notes: Fictional restaurant, supplier and cold-logistics company. Imported frozen fish undercutting lake fishermen is a real trade issue; no real business is depicted. Inspection signs are given only in outline.

ob.text: A cook reports the owner of a fish restaurant at Lwang'ni beach, Roselyne Nafula (51), found dead in her kitchen at 06:40 when he came to open up.

people.name: Roselyne Nafula
people.bio: Eighteen years frying whole tilapia at Lwang'ni. Marks every one of her kitchen tools with red tape.

facts.text: Roselyne Nafula was found dead in her kitchen at Lwang'ni at 06:40 by her cook.
Two head wounds. She lies behind her counter.
Her cash drawer still holds the night's takings: KSh 14,600.
The hook where her fish-gutting mallet always hangs is empty. Roselyne marks every kitchen tool with red tape.
Her PesaPap till: the last payment was at 21:40, from a diner.
Roselyne's post in the owners' group, last Wednesday: "Don't buy from Ephantus. Frozen imported fish sold as fresh." Thirty restaurants cancelled within two days.
Roselyne's notebook: "Lazarus — till short KSh 3,000 — warned him, deducted from wages." Marked settled.
Her receipts: every one of Ephantus's supply invoices is paid up to date.
County receipt: Roselyne owns the kitchen plot outright. There is no lease.
Hamisi: he pulled the front shutter at 22:05 and left. Roselyne was counting cash and said she'd prep tomorrow's onions. Sylvia's touts had fought with him earlier, "like every night".
Hamisi's PesaPap: a 22:07 tuk-tuk fare from Lwang'ni to Kondele.
Everlyne: Lazarus left with the other cooks at 22:00. They shared a tuk-tuk to Nyalenda and dropped him at his gate at 22:25, where his wife let him in.
Fisheries inspection, last Wednesday: five tilapia "supplied as fresh lake fish by E. Mwangi" were previously frozen imported fish.
Norah was off duty at home with her family on Tuesday evening from 18:00.
Truck GPS log: Ephantus's truck was at Lwang'ni from 22:10 to 22:35 on Tuesday night.
In the cold box of Ephantus's truck, among the frozen cartons: a fish-gutting mallet, frozen, with a strip of red tape on the handle.
Chama minutes: Sylvia took the minutes at a members' house in Milimani from 20:00 to 23:00.
Lazarus: "I took three thousand. She caught me and forgave me. She took it from my wages. I'd never touch her."
Sylvia: "Our boys fight every night. Roselyne and I drank tea together every morning."
Autopsy: two blows with a heavy round-headed object.
Autopsy: blood carbon monoxide normal; no water in the lungs.
Autopsy: death between 21:45 and 23:30.
Lab: blood preserved by the cold on the mallet head is Roselyne's.
Dr. Chebii: the mallet's round head matches both wounds.
Ephantus: "I haven't been to Lwang'ni since Friday. On Tuesday night I was delivering in town."
Ephantus: "That woman lied about my fish."
Ephantus admits he went to Roselyne's kitchen on Tuesday night "to ask her to take back what she wrote".
Ephantus: "She laughed. I left. She was counting money when I walked out."
Sylvia: "I was at my chama."
Lazarus: "I left at ten with the others."

interrogations.intro: Ephantus stands by his truck at the depot, arms crossed. "I haven't been to Lwang'ni since Friday. That woman lied about my fish and cost me everything."

topics.reply: Frozen, fresh, who can tell? Fish is fish. She wanted cheaper, she found an excuse.

interrogations.intro: Sylvia is already frying at her own kitchen next door, red-eyed. "Our boys fight. We don't."

topics.reply: Our boys fight every night. Roselyne and I drank tea together every morning. I was at my chama, I took the minutes. Here.

interrogations.intro: Lazarus sits on an upturned crate by the frying vat, not looking at the counter. "I left at ten with the others."

topics.reply: I took three thousand. She caught me and forgave me. She took it from my wages. I'd never touch her.

interrogations.intro: Hamisi leans his menu board against a table. "I closed the front at five past ten. She was counting the money."

topics.reply: He went with the other cooks, ten o'clock. Ask Everlyne next door, they share a tuk-tuk.

interrogations.intro: Norah brings the inspection photographs out of a folder. "She brought me five fish. All five had been frozen."

contradictions.reaction: He uncrosses his arms. "...I went to ask her to take back what she wrote. She laughed. I left. She was counting money."
Ephantus looks at the photograph of the frozen mallet with her red tape on it. "Thirty restaurants in two days," he says. "Thirty." He doesn't say anything else.

Alive and counting cash at 22:05; the truck was at Lwang'ni from 22:10 to 22:35, and its driver admits he was in her kitchen.

The cook was in a tuk-tuk at ten. He stole three thousand; he didn't kill her.

prosecutor.pass: Her own mallet, missing from its hook. Yes.

prosecutor.pass: Five fish on an inspector's tray and thirty cancelled orders. That's the reason.

timeOfDeath.note: Alive and counting cash at 22:05; the autopsy allows 21:45–23:30.

proof.concludes: The last diner paid at 21:40, the cooks left at 22:00, and at 22:05 Roselyne was alive and alone, counting the takings.
She had exposed Ephantus's "fresh lake fish" as imported frozen fish, and cost him thirty restaurants in two days.
Ephantus wasn't delivering in town: his truck was at Lwang'ni from 22:10 to 22:35, inside the window, and he admits he went to her kitchen.

Her red-taped mallet, missing from its hook, is frozen in his truck with her blood on it, and it matches both wounds. Ephantus Mwangi struck Roselyne with her own fish-gutting mallet because she'd exposed his frozen imported fish.

Lazarus left with the cooks at 22:00 and was dropped at his gate at 22:25.

Hamisi took a tuk-tuk to Kondele at 22:07.

The night's takings are still in the drawer.

That theft was found, deducted and forgiven, and it's Lazarus's matter.
She owned the kitchen plot outright.

reconstruction.text: Roselyne notices that Ephantus's "fresh lake tilapia" have flat cloudy eyes and ice crystals in the gills. She takes five to the county fisheries inspector: imported, frozen, thawed.
She posts the result in the owners' group. Within two days thirty restaurants cancel his supply.
Tuesday, 22:05. Hamisi pulls the shutter; Roselyne counts the takings alone. At 22:10 Ephantus's cold truck pulls in at the beach.
In her kitchen he demands a retraction. She refuses and laughs. He takes her gutting mallet from its hook and strikes her twice.
He hides the mallet in the cold box among the frozen fish and drives away at 22:35. The truck's GPS keeps the time for him.

clockPlan.note: One warrant on the truck. No detention needed. The trace result (12 h) breaks his second story.
